examples.subject: experiment: two-phase data-driven case factorization (10-min budget)
examples.note: train.py sets EXTENDED_TIME_BUDGET=600s replacing 300s budget; two-phase case-folding embedding experiment.
examples.message:
experiment: two-phase data-driven case factorization (10-min budget)

Phase 1 (3 min): Train standard model to learn token representations.
Phase 2 (7 min): Analyze trained embeddings to find which upper/lower
token pairs have similar representations (cosine > 0.3), fold those
pairs to share embeddings, add a learned case signal vector, then
continue training with fresh optimizer state.

This is data-driven semantic tokenization: the model itself decides
which tokens benefit from case folding, rather than applying it
blindly to all 841 case pairs.

examples.subject: experiment: extended BPE (case fold + 841 bigram merges, 10-min)
examples.note: Case-fold plus bigram-merge remap applied to train and val data; evaluate_bpb with overridden token_bytes.
examples.message:
experiment: extended BPE (case fold + 841 bigram merges, 10-min)

Case-fold 841 uppercase tokens into lowercase, then fill the freed
841 vocab slots with the most frequent token bigrams. Greedy
left-to-right bigram merging applied in the dataloader via remap_fn.
Merged tokens get summed byte counts for correct BPB evaluation.

This effectively extends the BPE vocabulary: same 8192 tokens but
the freed case slots now represent common bigrams, improving the
tokenizer's compression ratio.

examples.subject: fix: apply bigram merge at encode time (not packed sequence time)
examples.note: Moves case/bigram merge into prepare Tokenizer.post_encode_fn; eval keeps token_bytes override on remapped val.
examples.message:
fix: apply bigram merge at encode time (not packed sequence time)

The previous remap_fn approach padded merged sequences with -1,
creating a degenerate task where the model only predicted non-pad
tokens (train loss dropped to 0.015). Fix: apply case folding and
bigram merging at document encode time via Tokenizer.post_encode_fn.
The dataloader packer then naturally fills sequences with more text.

Also add post_encode_fn support to Tokenizer class in prepare.py.

examples.note: Switches to case-folded tokenizer; eval uses its token_bytes (shift tokens 0 bytes); 10-min budget.
examples.message:
experiment: case-folded BPE with shift tokens (10-min)

Use CaseFoldedTokenizer: BPE trained on lowercased text, with
SHIFT_CHAR and SHIFT_TOKEN inserted at encode time. "Hello",
"hello", "HELLO" all share the same BPE tokens. Better merges
from case-invariant training actually REDUCE token count by ~6%
despite shift token overhead.

examples.subject: P4u: gate_from_postlude0 — compute gate from first recurrence output
examples.note: gate_from_postlude0 variant; TIME_BUDGET override changed 80 to 20 min (x4).
examples.message:
P4u: gate_from_postlude0 — compute gate from first recurrence output

New gate variant: instead of gating from prelude output alone (e),
compute gate from cat[e, s_k0] where s_k0 = state after the forced
k=0 recurrence pass.

Key difference from gate_from_prelude:
- Gate sees HOW MUCH the first recurrence changed the token
- Tokens with small |s_k0 - e| likely don't need more recurrence
- Tokens with large |s_k0 - e| are still "updating" and may benefit
- Gradient flows through k=0 recur → gate → loss (richer than prelude-only)

gate_proj input: cat[e, s_k0] → shape (B, T, 2*H) → (B, T, 1)
Con

limitations: Selection: only forks whose owners pushed agent history; most runs (results.tsv is untracked by default) are invisible.
Discarded experiments are usually reset away before pushing, so per-class keep rates come only from the few commits joined to a committed results.tsv; the commit-level keep rate is biased upward.
A handful of forks dominate counts (see headline.eval_or_budget_by_fork); per-fork shares are more robust than pooled shares.
'who' (agent vs human) is a heuristic from author names, co-author trailers and message style; many agents commit under the operator's git identity.
'exp' vs 'setup' context is a judgement from messages, branch and diff size; operator-directed protocol changes can look like agent experiments.

Loss-path changes (label smoothing / z-loss / focal loss inside forward, which evaluate_bpb also sums) were not flagged by the main rules; they are counted by a separate regex and were not individually reviewed.
The fork listing covers 158 pages (oldest 1-129, newest 1-21, stargazers 1-8); forks created after the listing, deleted, or renamed are missed.
